newsitem.title: USA: Calif. pilot sought in cremated remains probe.
newsitem.headline: Calif. pilot sought in cremated remains probe.

text.p: Investigators searched on Sunday for a California pilot who allegedly put thousands of boxes of cremated human remains in storage rather than spread them over mountains and at sea.

The Contra Costa County Sheriff's Department said it had issued an arrest warrant for Allan Vieira, who operates the Vieira Flying Service. Authorities believe he was hired by funeral homes in California to spread the ashes over mountains, rivers and the Pacific Ocean.

Instead, deputies said Vieira placed at least 3,500 boxes of the cremated remains in public storage lockers in Discovery Bay, about 45 miles (72 km) east of San Francisco, and at a nearby hangar where he kept a plane.
Vieira could face a number of charges, including fraud, if he is found to be responsible for the remains, they said.
The macabre discovery shocked northern California residents and baffled investigators.

Most of the boxes of ashes have name tags and dates attached, identifying the deceased and when they were cremated. One box was dated in the 1950s. Investigators said some of the boxes had been opened.
"They were thrown in there (the lockers) like he didn't care," one investigator said.
Deputies said the boxes would be returned to the families of the deceased.
